mainTopic: Which foods are valid for an עירוב (the משנה's 'פשיטא' cases), and who may deliver an עירוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing a quote that the poor and troops may be fed דמאי, and רב הונא shows this follows בית הלל against בית שמאי. Next, the גמרא goes through each food on our משנה's list and asks 'פשיטא!', why say something obvious? Each time it finds a special case. מעשר ראשון taken while the grain was on the stalks never owes תרומה גדולה. This follows ריש לקיש, and אביי defends that reading against רב פפא, because only piled grain counts as 'דגן'. Redeemed food is valid even if the חומש is unpaid. Even טבל מדרבנן is invalid. Food redeemed improperly, with a blank coin or with land, stays unredeemed. Then a new משנה teaches that an עירוב sent with a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, or with someone who rejects עירוב, is invalid, unless a fit person receives it and places it. The גמרא explains that a קטן is unfit for עירובי תחומין but fit for עירובי חצירות. It also explains that the sender watches the carrier, and that we presume an agent does his job (חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו), tracing both answers to a ברייתא about an elephant and a monkey. Finally, רב נחמן limits that presumption: it is not relied on for Torah laws.

steps.title: Troops may also be fed דמאי
steps.stepSummary: This line ends a quoted source: just as the poor may be fed דמאי, so may traveling troops.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may also feed troops דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote it already started: 'We may feed the poor דמאי, and troops דמאי.' This supports the idea that a poor person may eat דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the quote is that דמאי is only a rabbinic doubt. So חז״ל went easy on it for the poor and for troops. That leniency is part of why דמאי can be used for an עירוב, since a person could make himself 'poor' by declaring his property הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ. It is unclear whether its tithes were taken.
Traveling troops or lodgers who must be fed.

phrases.english: and [one may feed] troops demai.
phrases.notes: The end of the quote from משנה דמאי (3:1) that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a quote that started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Troops, like the poor, may be fed דמאי.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about feeding the poor דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא: בית שמאי forbid feeding the poor דמאי, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A ברייתא taught: בית שמאי say we may not feed the poor דמאי. בית הלל say we may feed the poor דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a ברייתא showing that the rule 'we may feed the poor דמאי' is really a disagreement. The lenient rule we just saw follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, we might think everyone agrees the poor may eat דמאי. רב הונא shows that בית שמאי disagree. The rule follows בית הלל, as it usually does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
The students of שמאי. Their view is usually stricter.
The students of הלל. The הלכה usually follows them.
We may feed (others).

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It was taught:
Beit Shammai say:
One may not feed the poor demai,
and Beit Hillel say:
One may feed the poor demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the rule in step 1 is a מחלוקת, and that it follows בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל allow feeding the poor דמאי. בית שמאי forbid it.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that the poor may eat דמאי follows בית הלל. This is part of why דמאי can be used for an עירוב.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to mention מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks: isn't it obvious that it is fine once its תרומה was taken?
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] 'And with מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, etc.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in our משנה. It asks why the משנה bothers to teach something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the gifts were already taken from the מעשר ראשון, it is plain חולין and fine for an עירוב. So the גמרא pushes to find what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The first tithe, given to the לוי.
'It is obvious!' A challenge that a teaching seems unnecessary.
'Etc.' The rest of the quote is left out.

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא is not saying the משנה is wrong. It is only asking what new point the משנה is teaching.

phrases.english: [We learned:] 'And with first tithe whose [teruma] was taken, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה, which opens a new topic.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from דמאי to the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to teach that מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken may be used for an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Produce whose gifts were taken is plain חולין, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case is where the לוי took his tithe while the grain was still on the stalks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a case where the לוי took his מעשר before the כהן took תרומה גדולה. Only תרומת מעשר was taken from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he took it early, while the grain was still on the stalks. תרומת מעשר was taken from it, but תרומה גדולה was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the פשיטא. The משנה is talking about an unusual case. The לוי got his tithe before the כהן took his share, so it seems to still owe תרומה גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally תרומה גדולה comes first, so a part of the לוי's tithe should have gone to the כהן. The משנה's חידוש is that even so, this מעשר is fine for an עירוב once only תרומת מעשר is taken. It does not still owe תרומה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for…' This brings a narrower case to answer a פשיטא.
He took it early, ahead of the usual order.
Stalks or ears of grain, before threshing.
The main תרומה given to the כהן from the crop.
The tenth of his מעשר that the לוי gives to the כהן.

phrases.english: It is only necessary
where he took it first, while it was on the stalks,
and the teruma of the tithe was taken from it,
but the great teruma was not taken from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a narrower case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seems obvious: all gifts were taken, so it is plain חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is מעשר taken early on the stalks, so תרומה גדולה was never taken. It is still valid.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows ריש לקיש, as reported by רבי אבהו. מעשר ראשון taken early on the stalks does not owe תרומה גדולה, and he brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows what רבי אבהו said in the name of ריש לקיש. מעשר ראשון that was taken early on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה, as the פסוק says: 'And you shall set apart from it a gift for ה׳, a tenth of the tithe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the basis for its answer. ריש לקיש rules that מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks owes no תרומה גדולה, and he brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the מעשר in step 4 is fine for an עירוב even though תרומה גדולה was never taken: it never owed it. Taking it 'on the stalks' matters because grain does not owe תרומה גדולה until it is threshed and piled.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports teachings of ריש לקיש.
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, a major אמורא of ארץ ישראל.
Exempt.
'As it is said.' This introduces a פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the הלכה behind the case in the משנה: a לוי who takes his tithe early on the stalks does not have to give תרומה גדולה from it.

phrases.english: And this follows what Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Reish Lakish:
First tithe that [the Levite] took first, on the stalks,
is exempt from the great teruma,
as it is said: 'And you shall set apart from it a gift for the Lord,
a tithe from the tithe.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר ראשון taken early on the stalks does not need תרומה גדולה taken from it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's ruling, based on במדבר יח:כו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה.

steps.title: The verse says only מעשר מן המעשר, not תרומה גדולה too
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק tells the לוי to separate only 'a tithe from the tithe,' which is תרומת מעשר. It does not tell him to separate תרומה גדולה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A tithe from the tithe' is what I told you to separate. I did not tell you to separate תרומה גדולה and also תרומת מעשר from the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: This explains how the פסוק proves ריש לקיש's rule. The Torah requires only one gift from the לוי's tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מעשר מן המעשר' limit the לוי's duty to תרומת מעשר alone. So if he got his tithe before תרומה גדולה became due, he owes nothing more than תרומת מעשר. That is why the מעשר in our משנה may be used for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I told you.' The Torah is pictured as speaking to the לוי.
'A tithe from the tithe.' This means תרומת מעשר.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case is מעשר ראשון taken on the stalks. It only needs תרומת מעשר, because the פסוק requires just 'a tithe from the tithe.' So once that is taken, it may be used for an עירוב.

phrases.english: 'A tithe from the tithe' I told you,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: and not the great teruma and the teruma of the tithe from the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 5 proves the rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לוי owes only תרומת מעשר from tithe he took on the stalks. So the case in our משנה is valid for an עירוב.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: then exempt the grain pile too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי. By the same reasoning, a לוי who took his מעשר after the grain was piled should also be exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, then even if the לוי took his share first when the grain was already in a pile, he should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the reading of the פסוק from the last step. He shows that it seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the לוי gives only 'a tithe from the tithe.' If that is the whole rule, it should apply no matter when the לוי took his מעשר. That would include after threshing, when the grain sits in a pile (כרי). But the challenge assumes that in the pile case the לוי does owe תרומה גדולה, so the reading seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: a standard opener for a challenge
He went before him: the לוי took his מעשר before the כהן took תרומה
A pile of threshed grain, the last stage of processing

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּימוֹ בִּכְרִי נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, even if he went first when it was in the pile, it should also be exempt!
phrases.notes: That is, the לוי took his מעשר after the grain was threshed and piled, but before the כהן took תרומה גדולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּימוֹ בִּכְרִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the פסוק given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the לוי owes only תרומת מעשר and never תרומה גדולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof is too broad. It would also exempt the pile case, where we know תרומה גדולה is owed.

steps.title: אביי answers with another verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a different פסוק, 'from all your tithes,' requires תרומה גדולה in the pile case.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: About your case, the פסוק says: 'From all your tithes you shall set apart all of ה׳'s תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא by bringing a second פסוק. This פסוק covers exactly the pile case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from all' (מכל) widen the rule. They teach that a לוי must sometimes give the full תרומה, meaning תרומה גדולה, from his מעשר. אביי applies that to the pile case. Now there are two פסוקים, one that exempts and one that requires.

keyTerms.meaning: About you (your case), the פסוק says
From all your tithes: an inclusive wording that adds a case

phrases.english: He said to him: About your case, the verse says:
"From all your tithes you shall separate
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:כט, read here together with the nearby פסוק about tithes.

phrases.english: all of ה׳'s teruma."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a second פסוק that covers the challenged case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'tithe from the tithe' פסוק exempts the לוי in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate פסוק, 'from all,' requires תרומה גדולה in the pile case.

steps.title: Why apply each verse this way?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks how אביי decided which פסוק covers which case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to make you assign the verses this way?
steps.whatsHappening: With two פסוקים pulling in opposite directions, the גמרא asks why the stalks case gets the exemption and the pile case gets the requirement. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ומה ראית' means: why not the other way around? Without a reason, splitting the cases between the two פסוקים looks random. The question asks for a logical basis.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? A request for the reason behind a choice

phrases.english: And what did you see (to divide it this way)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the two פסוקים were divided between the two cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of the exempting פסוק to the stalks and the requiring פסוק to the pile.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a reason, the split could just as easily be reversed.

steps.title: Piled grain counts as grain; grain on stalks does not
steps.stepSummary: Once grain is piled it is called 'דגן,' so תרומה גדולה applies. Grain still on the stalks is not yet דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (in the pile) has become grain, and that one (on the stalks) has not become grain.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason for the split. It depends on whether the produce has become 'grain' yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah ties the duty of תרומה to 'your grain' (דגנך). Threshed grain in a pile has reached that stage, so תרומה גדולה was already owed before the לוי took his share. On the stalks it is not yet דגן, so the לוי's early share was taken before that duty began.

keyTerms.meaning: It has become grain (דגן): fully processed
It has not yet become grain

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר ראשון taken while the grain is on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. Taken after the grain is piled, it is not exempt. The difference is whether the produce is already 'דגן.'

phrases.english: This one has become grain,
phrases.notes: Threshed and piled in a כרי.

phrases.english: and that one has not become grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by giving a real difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a real difference in the produce's stage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split between the פסוקים looks random.
steps.terutzMaskana: Becoming דגן is what triggers תרומה גדולה, so the pile owes it and the stalks do not.

steps.title: Isn't redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש obviously allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case and asks why it needed to be taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may make an עירוב with מעשר שני and הקדש that were redeemed. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה. It asks why this needed saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once מעשר שני or הקדש is redeemed, it becomes ordinary food. Ordinary food can obviously be used for an עירוב, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: eaten in ירושלים unless redeemed for money
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
That were redeemed: their holiness was moved onto money
It is obvious! A challenge that a ruling is unnecessary

phrases.english: And (one may make an eruv) with second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of מעשר ראשון and turns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling allowing redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeemed food is ordinary food, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A missing חומש does not hold back the redemption
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the redeemer paid the main value but not the added fifth. The food still counts as redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where he paid the main value but not the added fifth. The משנה teaches that the fifth does not hold back the redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה is about a special case. This case is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner who redeems his own מעשר שני or הקדש must add a fifth (חומש). One might think the redemption is not complete until the חומש is paid. The משנה teaches that paying the main value (קרן) is enough to make the food ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for: introduces the special case
The main value of the item
The added fifth an owner pays when redeeming his own item
Holds back or blocks the result

steps.confusionAlert: The חומש is still owed! It just does not block the food from becoming ordinary food.

phrases.english: It is only needed where he paid the principal
but did not pay the (added) fifth.
And it teaches us
that the fifth does not hold back (the redemption).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁנָּתַן אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְלֹא נָתַן אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by limiting the משנה to a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of a full, ordinary redemption, which would be obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a case where the חומש is unpaid, and teaches that it does not block the redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of פדיון: אין החומש מעכב.

steps.title: Isn't טבל obviously not allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that טבל cannot be used for an עירוב and asks why it needed saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may not make an עירוב with טבל. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next phrase of the משנה. It again asks why this needed to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is produce whose תרומות and מעשרות were not yet taken. It is forbidden to eat, and an עירוב must be food one is allowed to eat, so the ruling seems obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce whose תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been separated

phrases.english: But not with tevel.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 11, applied to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבל is forbidden to eat, so obviously it cannot serve as an עירוב.

steps.title: The case is טבל that is forbidden only by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking of טבל מדרבנן, such as produce grown in a pot with no hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for טבל that is only forbidden by the Rabbis, for example where he planted it in a pot without a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה is speaking of a lighter kind of טבל. Here the ruling is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, produce grown in a pot with no hole (עציץ שאינו נקוב) is not counted as growing from the ground, so it is not טבל at all. The Rabbis still required tithing it. The משנה teaches that even this rabbinic טבל cannot be used for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Counted as טבל only by rabbinic law
A plant pot with no hole, so it is not connected to the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Each 'obvious' ruling in the משנה teaches a hidden point. A redemption is complete without the חומש. Even טבל מדרבנן cannot be used for an עירוב.

phrases.english: It is only needed for tevel that is tevel by rabbinic law,
for example, where he planted it in a pot without a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by limiting the משנה to a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of Torah-level טבל, which would be obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of טבל מדרבנן and teaches that it too is not valid for an עירוב.

steps.title: Why teach that מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken cannot be used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that first tithe whose תרומה was not taken cannot be used for an עירוב, and asks why this needed saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with first tithe whose תרומה was not taken.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the משנה's list and asks why the משנה bothered to state it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תרומה was not taken from first tithe, the food is still טבל, and טבל may not be eaten. The משנה already said טבל cannot be used for an עירוב, so this line seems to repeat a known rule.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe: the tenth of the produce given to the לוי
The portion of produce given to the כהן
It is obvious! (Why say it?)

phrases.english: And not with first tithe
whose teruma was not taken.
It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The challenge: this is simply טבל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as steps 11 and 13, now applied to the next item in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about first tithe whose תרומה was not taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such produce is plainly טבל, which is forbidden to eat, so the ruling looks unnecessary

steps.title: The case: the לוי took his tithe from the pile first
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the לוי took his tithe from the grain pile before the כהן took תרומה גדולה. Only תרומת מעשר was taken, not תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed where the לוי got there first, at the pile. תרומת מעשר was taken from it, but תרומה גדולה was not taken from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a specific case where the ruling is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן's תרומה גדולה is taken first, and then the לוי's tithe. Here the לוי took his tithe from the pile before the כהן received anything. The לוי separated תרומת מעשר from his share, but he never separated the תרומה גדולה that sits inside that tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a special case)
He preceded him (the לוי came before the כהן)
A pile of grain that has been threshed and gathered
The tenth of his tithe that the לוי gives to a כהן
The main תרומה, separated first from all produce

phrases.english: It is only needed
where he (the Levite) preceded him (the priest) at the pile,
and teruma of the tithe was taken from it
but teruma gedola was not taken from it.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of תרומה. תרומת מעשר is the לוי's tenth-of-a-tenth, and it WAS taken. תרומה גדולה is the כהן's main portion, and it was NOT taken.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limits the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to repeat the plain rule against טבל
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to first tithe taken from the pile before תרומה גדולה, where it is not obvious that it is still טבל

steps.title: The משנה follows אביי, not רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought, like רב פפא, that the לוי is exempt from תרומה גדולה here. The משנה teaches, like אביי's answer, that he is not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the law is as רב פפא said to אביי. The משנה teaches us as אביי answered him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new lesson the משנה teaches in this case by tying it to the earlier argument between רב פפא and אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא argued that a לוי who comes first is exempt from תרומה גדולה, so his tithe would be usable for an עירוב. אביי answered, as in step 10, that this exemption applies only to grain still on the stalks. Once grain is piled it is 'דגן' and owes תרומה גדולה. The משנה confirms אביי's answer: the food is still טבל and is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (the actual new point)
As he answered him

steps.whatToRemember: First tithe taken from the pile before תרומה גדולה is still טבל and cannot be used for an עירוב. This follows אביי's answer that piled grain is 'דגן.'

phrases.english: Lest you say
as Rav Pappa said to Abaye,
phrases.notes: That the Levite is exempt from תרומה גדולה

phrases.english: it teaches us as he (Abaye) answered him.
phrases.notes: In the pile it is 'דגן' and owes תרומה גדולה

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the משנה to settle the earlier exchange, and it rules that a לוי who takes his tithe from the pile is not exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כְּדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 16 by spelling out its new lesson
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the new lesson by stating the mistaken first thought
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב פפא, the לוי would be exempt, so the food would be permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: Following אביי, piled grain owes תרומה גדולה, so the food is טבל

steps.title: Why teach that unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש cannot be used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about second tithe and הקדש that were not redeemed, and asks why this needed saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with second tithe or הקדש that were not redeemed.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and again asks why it needed to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unredeemed מעשר שני may not be eaten outside ירושלים. Unredeemed הקדש belongs to the Temple. Neither seems usable for an עירוב, so the ruling looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed for money
Property dedicated to the Temple
They were redeemed (exchanged for money)

phrases.english: And not with second tithe or consecrated food
that were not redeemed.
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge pattern, applied to a new item in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unredeemed holy food is plainly forbidden for ordinary use, so the ruling looks unnecessary

steps.title: Redeemed improperly, as with an unminted coin
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed where he did redeem them, but not properly. An example is מעשר שני redeemed with an אסימון, a blank coin. The Torah requires money with a stamped image.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed where he redeemed them, but not according to the law. For מעשר, this is where he redeemed it with an unminted coin, and the Torah says 'וצרת הכסף': money that has an image (צורה) on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a case where a redemption was attempted but was not valid. It gives the example for מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think any redemption attempt is enough to release the food. The גמרא reads 'וצרת' as connected to 'צורה,' an image. So only a minted coin can redeem מעשר שני, and a blank אסימון does not work. The food stays unredeemed and cannot be used for an עירוב. The case for הקדש comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their law (properly)
An unminted coin: a metal blank with no image stamped on it
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
'And you shall bind up the money' (דברים יד:כה)
An image or form stamped on a coin

steps.whatToRemember: An attempt to redeem מעשר שני only works with a valid minted coin. With an אסימון, the food is still unredeemed and cannot be used for an עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: The new point is not that unredeemed food is forbidden, since that is obvious. The new point is that a faulty redemption counts as no redemption at all.

phrases.english: It is only needed where he redeemed them,
but did not redeem them properly:
Tithe, where he redeemed it with an unminted coin,
and the Torah said: 'And you shall bind up the money,'
meaning money that has a form on it.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that only a minted coin can redeem מעשר שני.
steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁפְּדָאָן, וְלֹא פְּדָאָן כְּהִלְכָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 18 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא with a verse reading: a faulty redemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to teach only that fully unredeemed food is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Even where redemption was attempted, an invalid method (an אסימון) leaves the food unredeemed

steps.title: הקדש redeemed with land
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the answer from step 19. The משנה's case of unredeemed הקדש means הקדש that was 'redeemed' with land. That does not work, because the Torah says the redemption must be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And הקדש means a case where he redeemed it with land. The Torah says: 'He shall give the money and it shall be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in the last step. It now gives the case for הקדש: someone tried to redeem it with land instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 explained 'not redeemed' as 'redeemed, but not properly.' For מעשר שני the bad redemption was a blank coin. For הקדש the bad redemption is land, because the פסוק says 'money' (כסף). Since the redemption fails, the food is still הקדש and cannot be used for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that was consecrated to the בית המקדש
He redeemed it, moving its holiness onto something else
Onto land
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases in the משנה mean 'redeemed, but improperly.' מעשר שני was redeemed with a blank coin, and הקדש was redeemed with land. Neither redemption works, so neither food can be used for an עירוב.

phrases.english: Consecrated property — where he redeemed it onto land,
for the Merciful One said:
"He shall give the money and it shall be his."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same answer begun in step 19 (מעשר שני, then הקדש).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly (אוקימתא): improper redemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might think redeeming הקדש with land of equal value would work
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires money, so redeeming with land fails and the food stays הקדש

steps.title: משנה: sending an עירוב with an unfit messenger
steps.stepSummary: If someone sends his עירוב with a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, or with someone who does not accept עירוב, it is not valid. If he told another person to receive it from that messenger and place it, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sends his עירוב with a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor, or with someone who does not accept עירוב, it is not an עירוב. But if he told another person to receive it from him, it is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches who may deliver and place an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is that a competent person who accepts עירוב places it in the right spot. An unfit messenger cannot do this himself. But if a fit person takes the food from him and places it, the עירוב works, because it does not matter how the food got there.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, minor. These are the three people treated as legally incompetent.
Someone who does not accept the law of עירוב
To receive it from him

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who sends his eiruv
in the hand of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּיַד מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בְּעֵירוּב —
phrases.english: or in the hand of one who does not accept eiruv —
it is not an eiruv.
But if he told another person
to receive it from him —
this is an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ עֵירוּבוֹ בְּיַד חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, starting a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב placed by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, or by someone who rejects עירוב, is invalid. It is valid if a fit person receives it from them and places it.

steps.title: Challenge: רב הונא says a קטן may collect an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say a קטן is unfit. רב הונא said a קטן may collect the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is a minor really not fit? But רב הונא said: a minor may collect the עירוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling about a קטן. It quotes רב הונא, who seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an עירוב sent with a קטן is invalid. רב הונא says a קטן may even gather the food for an עירוב from the neighbors. That suggests a קטן is fit to handle an עירוב, so the two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say! This introduces a contradicting source.
Collects
An אמורא who taught the law about a קטן collecting an עירוב

phrases.english: Gemara:
And a minor is not [fit]?
But didn't Rav Huna say:
A minor may collect the eiruv!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one detail of the משנה in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a קטן cannot deliver an עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction from רב הונא, who allows a קטן to collect an עירוב

steps.title: Answer: עירובי תחומין versus עירובי חצירות
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The משנה is about עירובי תחומין, and רב הונא is about עירובי חצירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the משנה is talking about an עירוב for שבת boundaries. There, רב הונא is talking about an עירוב for courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. It shows that each source is talking about a different kind of עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירובי תחומין sets up a new 'home base' for שבת. That is more serious, so a קטן cannot do it. An עירובי חצירות only joins homes that already exist. That is more lenient, so a קטן can collect and place it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
An עירוב that extends how far you may walk on שבת
An עירוב that joins courtyard homes so you may carry between them

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying a קטן is fit for every עירוב. He is only fit for עירובי חצירות. For עירובי תחומין, which the משנה is discussing, he is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two kinds of עירוב have different strictness, and that affects who may set them up.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, regarding an eiruv of borders;
there, regarding an eiruv of courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּעֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין, כָּאן בְּעֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into different cases (כאן... כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רב הונא seem to disagree about whether a קטן is fit
steps.terutzMaskana: A קטן is unfit for עירובי תחומין but fit for עירובי חצירות

steps.title: Who is 'one who does not accept עירוב'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'one who does not accept עירוב' and asks who that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Or with someone who does not accept עירוב.' Who is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the משנה. It asks who that phrase is talking about, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request to identify the person. The משנה gave a description, and the גמרא wants to know which group it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְּיַד מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בְּעֵירוּב.
phrases.english: "Or in the hand of one who does not accept eiruv."
Who [is this]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ בְּיַד מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בְּעֵירוּב. מַאן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to clarify a different phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of person is meant by 'one who does not accept עירוב'

steps.title: רב חסדא: it means a כותי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the phrase means a כותי, a Samaritan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Samaritans (כותים).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from the last step. The person who does not accept עירוב is a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כותים keep the written Torah but do not accept the rabbinic law of עירוב. Since they do not believe in it, they cannot be trusted to set one up properly.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who identifies the person in the משנה
Samaritans (כותים), who reject many rabbinic laws

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Samaritans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'One who does not accept עירוב' means a כותי

steps.title: Quoting the end of the משנה about another person receiving the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that if the sender told another person to receive the עירוב from the unfit carrier, the עירוב is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if he told another person to receive it from him, it is a valid עירוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה to set up a question about it. This step is a setup for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said a חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot deliver an עירוב. Here it adds a fix: a fit adult takes the עירוב from the carrier and places it. The גמרא will now test whether this fix really works.

keyTerms.meaning: to receive it from him (from the unfit carrier)
this is a valid עירוב
to another (fit) person

phrases.english: And if he told another person to receive it from him,
phrases.notes: 'From him' means from the חרש, שוטה, or קטן carrying it.

phrases.english: it is a valid eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining 'one who does not accept עירוב' to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב sent through an unfit carrier is valid if a fit person was told to receive it and place it.

steps.title: Maybe the carrier never delivers it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we should worry that the unfit carrier will not bring the עירוב to the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he will not bring it to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's ruling. A קטן or שוטה might never reach the person who is supposed to receive the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The receiver is reliable, but the carrier is not. If the carrier loses the food or wanders off, the receiver has nothing to place. So how can the משנה call it a valid עירוב?

keyTerms.meaning: and let us be concerned
perhaps
he will not bring it to him

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he will not bring it to him?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the unfit carrier; 'him' is the appointed receiver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the עירוב is valid when another person receives it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unreliable carrier may fail to deliver, so nothing guarantees the עירוב reaches the receiver.

steps.title: The sender stands and watches
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא's principle, the גמרא answers that the sender stands and watches until the carrier reaches the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said, it is a case where he stands and watches him. Here too, he stands and watches him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry. The sender watches the carrier the whole way, so he knows it was delivered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Delivery is not taken on trust. The sender sees it with his own eyes. The גמרא borrows רב חסדא's answer from another case, which steps 31–34 identify.

keyTerms.meaning: as (so-and-so) said
where he stands and watches him
here too

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥisda said: where he stands and watches him,
here too, it is where he stands and watches him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to a case where the sender watches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sender just hands off the עירוב and hopes it arrives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sender watches until the carrier reaches the receiver, so delivery is certain.

steps.title: Maybe the receiver never takes it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: perhaps the appointed receiver will not take the עירוב from the carrier and place it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he will not take it from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second worry. The sender saw the carrier arrive, but from far away he cannot see whether the receiver actually took the עירוב and placed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watching from a distance solves only the delivery. The last step, taking and placing the עירוב, is still unseen. So the problem moves to the receiver.

keyTerms.meaning: he will not take it from him

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he will not take it from him?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the appointed receiver; 'him' is the carrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 28 but points to a gap it does not cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of the עירוב even after the answer of 'he stands and watches'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Watching from afar does not confirm that the receiver actually took the עירוב and placed it.

steps.title: An agent is presumed to do his job
steps.stepSummary: Using רב יחיאל's principle, the גמרא answers that we presume an agent carries out his mission.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יחיאל said: there is a חזקה that an agent does his mission. Here too, there is a חזקה that the agent does his mission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second worry. The receiver is a proper שליח, and we assume a שליח does what he was asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we rely on a legal presumption instead of eyesight. The receiver is a fit adult, so we trust that he took the עירוב and placed it. Together the two answers cover the whole chain: we see the delivery, and we presume the placing.

keyTerms.meaning: a legal presumption
an agent
carries out his mission

steps.whatToRemember: Two worries, two answers: delivery is seen (בעומד ורואהו), and placing is presumed (חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו).

phrases.english: As Rav Yeḥiel said:
There is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי — חֲזָקָה שָׁלִיחַ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: here too, there is a presumption that the agent carries out his mission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without seeing it, we cannot know that the receiver took the עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fit agent is presumed to fulfill his mission, so we assume he took and placed it.

steps.title: Where were these two rulings first said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the statements of רב חסדא and רב יחיאל were originally said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where were the rulings of רב חסדא and רב יחיאל said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא borrowed two rulings, so now it asks for their original setting. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question of source, not an attack. Knowing the original case shows that these rulings were made for exactly this kind of situation: an unreliable carrier and a fit receiver.

keyTerms.meaning: and where was it said?

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵיכָא אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יְחִיאֵל?
phrases.english: And where were the statements of Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yeḥiel said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the two principles used in steps 28 and 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of the rulings of רב חסדא and רב יחיאל.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the elephant and the monkey
steps.stepSummary: The rulings were said on a ברייתא: an עירוב sent with an elephant or a monkey is invalid, but it is valid if another person was told to receive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were said on this, as a ברייתא teaches: if he gave it to an elephant and it brought it, or to a monkey and it brought it, it is not a valid עירוב. But if he told another person to receive it from the animal, it is a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting the ברייתא where the two rulings were first said. It is a case just like ours, except that the carrier is an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal cannot be a שליח, just as a קטן cannot here. The same fix works in both cases: a fit person receives the עירוב. So the same two worries came up there too.

keyTerms.meaning: it was said about this
as a ברייתא teaches
elephant
monkey
and it brought it

phrases.english: They were said about this, as it was taught in a baraita:
If he gave it to an elephant and it brought it,
or to a monkey and it brought it, it is not a valid eruv.
But if he told another person to receive it from it,
it is a valid eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא about an עירוב sent with an elephant or a monkey.

steps.title: In the original case: maybe the animal never delivers it
steps.stepSummary: On the ברייתא, the original question was raised: perhaps the animal will not bring the עירוב to the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it will not bring it to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the first question as it was originally asked about the ברייתא. The animal might not reach the receiver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same worry as in step 27, but here it is in its original place. The גמרא repeats it to show where רב חסדא's answer came from.

phrases.english: But perhaps it will not bring it to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the original challenge on the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the עירוב is valid when another person receives it from the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal may not deliver the food to the receiver.

steps.title: רב חסדא's original answer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answered that the case is where the sender stands and watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is where he stands and watches it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב חסדא's answer in its original place. The sender watches the animal until it reaches the receiver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the answer used in step 28 was first made for an unreliable carrier, so applying it to a קטן fits naturally.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: where he stands and watches it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal is sent off with no one watching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sender watches, so delivery is certain.

steps.title: In the original case: maybe the receiver never accepts it
steps.stepSummary: On the ברייתא, the second question was raised: perhaps the receiver will not accept the עירוב from the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he will not accept it from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the second question as it was originally asked about the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watching from far away still does not show whether the receiver took the עירוב and placed it. This is the same gap as in step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: he will not accept it

phrases.english: But perhaps he will not accept it from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the remaining gap after step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling, even with the sender watching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The receiver's taking and placing of the עירוב is not seen.

steps.title: רב יחיאל's original answer
steps.stepSummary: רב יחיאל answered that there is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יחיאל said: there is a חזקה that an agent does his mission.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב יחיאל's answer in its original place. The receiver is a שליח, and we presume he did his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this, the source is complete. Both answers the גמרא borrowed earlier were made for this very ברייתא about animals.

phrases.english: Rav Yeḥiel said:
There is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We must see the receiver take the עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שליח is presumed to fulfill his mission.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits the agent presumption
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that for Torah-level laws, we do not rely on the presumption that an agent carries out his mission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: in matters of Torah law, there is no חזקה that an agent does his mission.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a limit to רב יחיאל's rule. The presumption works only in rabbinic matters, not in Torah-level ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Torah law, you must actually know the agent did the job; a presumption is not enough. עירוב is rabbinic, so the presumption can be relied on here. This explains why רב יחיאל's answer worked in our case.

keyTerms.meaning: in matters of Torah law
there is no presumption

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that an agent is presumed to do his job holds for rabbinic laws like עירוב, but רב נחמן says not for Torah laws.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the boundary of an important general rule about שליחות. The leniency in our sugya works because עירוב is a rabbinic law.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁל תּוֹרָה — אֵין חֲזָקָה שָׁלִיחַ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: In matters of Torah law, there is no presumption that an agent carries out his mission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the presumption of רב יחיאל used in steps 30 and 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presumption that an agent fulfills his mission is not relied upon for Torah-level laws.
